variants: AF-VIAL-LIQ: Aseptically filled solution in vials. Sequence: sterilizing filtration, aseptic filling and stoppering in Grade A (isolator, closed/open RABS or conventional A-in-B), then capping as an aseptic or clean process under Grade A air supply. Sources: EU GMP Annex 1 (2022) 8.7-8.29, FDA aseptic guidance (2004).

AF-AMP: Aseptically filled glass ampoules, fusion (flame) sealed. Annex 1 8.22 makes 100% integrity testing mandatory for fusion-sealed containers of 100 mL or less, and visual inspection does not count as an integrity test.

AF-PFS: Aseptically filled prefilled syringes and cartridges from ready-to-use nested tubs. Steps: tub and bag surface decontamination on transfer, filling, plunger stoppering by vacuum or vent tube, then secondary assembly (plunger rod, backstop, needle-safety device, labels). The assembled syringe is a combination product in the US (21 CFR Part 4) and a drug-device combination in the EU.

AF-LYO: Aseptically filled and lyophilized in vials. Steps: partial stoppering, Grade A transfer and loading, freeze-drying, in-chamber stoppering under sterile-filtered gas, unloading and capping. Annex 1 8.121-8.126 treats the lyophilizer as an extension of the aseptic process.

TS-MH-SVP: Terminally sterilized small-volume parenterals (vials or ampoules) by moist heat. Bulk is prepared in Grade D (Grade C if at unusual risk) and filled in Grade C (Grade A with C background if at unusual risk). Sterilization uses saturated steam, air-steam mixture or superheated water. Ph. Eur. 5.1.1 sets minimum F0 at 8 min in the slowest-to-heat position; the reference cycle is 121 °C for 15 min.

TS-MH-LVP: Terminally sterilized large-volume parenterals (bags or bottles, including FFS/BFS) using air-overpressure or superheated-water cycles. Annex 1 8.22 requires 100% integrity testing for fusion-sealed units of 100 mL or less; reduced sampling above 100 mL needs justification. Annex 1 8.62 requires cycle design that prevents container distortion.

AC-SUSP/EMUL (brief): Aseptically compounded non-filterable suspensions and emulsions. All components and equipment are sterilized and the product is compounded and filled in Grade A with Grade B background (Annex 1 8.11, 8.13). Lipid emulsions may instead be terminally sterilized. Emulsion critical quality attributes are globule size (USP <729>: MDD <500 nm, PFAT5 ≤0.05%) and homogeneity during filling.
OPTIONAL (not detailed): aseptic BFS (Annex 1 8.105-8.120) and sterile powder filling. These use the same framework, with extra CPPs for extrusion, parison and powder handling.

SPECIAL RECORD TYPE: Aseptic Process Simulation (media fill) batch record for each aseptic variant. PDA TR22 (Revised 2025) says it should use the same format and data requirements as the commercial record, and be electronic if the commercial record is electronic.

unit_operations.name: Batch record issuance and sterility-assurance pre-start gate
unit_operations.purpose: Create the executed BMR/BPR from the approved, effective master for the exact product, batch size, line and market(s). Block any GMP step until all sterility-assurance preconditions are verified: APS coverage, personnel qualification, cleanroom/utility/equipment status, and EM readiness.
bmr_records: Master record ID/version/effective date, product name, strength, dosage form, container-closure system, nominal fill volume, batch size (L or kg and theoretical units), unique batch number, intended market(s) (these select the EU/US rule pack), site/line/rooms with cleanroom grade and barrier type (isolator / closed RABS / open RABS / conventional A in B) [21 CFR 211.186(b), 211.188(a); EU GMP Ch.4 4.17/4.20]
Statement that the executed record is an accurate reproduction of the master, checked, dated and e-signed [21 CFR 211.188(a)]

Last successful APS (media fill) covering this line, process type, container/closure bracket, line-speed range, maximum filling duration, maximum number of personnel and each planned shift: APS IDs, dates, next due date (~6 months) [Annex 1 9.36, 9.38; FDA 2004 IX.A.2]

Grade A/B personnel roster: gowning qualification date and expiry (reassessed at least annually, with visual and microbial assessment), last successful APS participation (at least annually), training on this MBR and its SOPs, any disqualification status [Annex 1 7.4-7.6, 9.38; FDA 2004 V.A, IX.A.2]

Cleanroom and clean-air equipment status: last requalification (Grade A/B ≤6 months, Grade C/D ≤12 months), final-filter integrity, open maintenance work orders and return-to-use approvals for sterility-critical equipment [Annex 1 4.32, 5.6, 5.7]

Instrument and equipment status: calibration due dates (balances, particle counters, sterilizer control/monitor probes, filter integrity testers, pH/osmometer/densitometer), worst-case heat-sterilization load revalidated within 12 months [Annex 1 8.39; 21 CFR 211.68(a), 211.160(b)(4)]

Utilities status: WFI released (latest microbiological/endotoxin results, continuous TOC and conductivity in limits, loop temperature e.g. circulation >70 °C), clean steam periodic quality tests (condensate meets WFI monograph; non-condensable gases, dryness, superheat), process gas quality and point-of-use sterilizing filter status [Annex 1 6.10-6.19]
Room cleaning/disinfection status, including date of last sporicidal disinfection, disinfectant lot and in-use expiry (disinfectants must be sterile for Grade A/B) [Annex 1 4.33-4.35]
EM plan instantiated for the batch (locations, methods, frequencies, incubation conditions), media lots growth-promotion tested, continuous particle counters online [Annex 1 9.4-9.5, 9.17, 10.9]
Room/line clearance: previous product, batch and documents removed; checklist, performer, verifier [EU GMP Ch.5 5.40 (not independently verified here); 21 CFR 211.130(e)]
Open deviations, change controls and CAPA affecting the line or product, each acknowledged with a QA decision
critical_process_parameters: None (administrative gate). The gate conditions are hard stops: valid APS coverage, qualified personnel, requalified cleanrooms, calibrated critical instruments, released utilities.

in_process_controls.frequency: At batch creation and at start of each aseptic shift/session
in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Successful APS within the periodic window (twice a year, roughly every 6 months, per line, process and shift), covering container size, line speed, duration, interventions and personnel count [Annex 1 9.36, 9.38; FDA 2004 IX.A.2]
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Block batch start; no ad-hoc override; deviation plus QA decision per procedure

in_process_controls.frequency: Every entry into Grade B and before any Grade A intervention
in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Gowning qualification current (≤12 months), APS participation ≤12 months, not disqualified [Annex 1 7.4, 7.6, 9.38]
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Deny unsupervised entry. Exceptional supervised entry of an unqualified person only per written procedure, recorded with an impact assessment [Annex 1 7.5]

in_process_controls.frequency: At batch start and at each shift change
in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: All requalifications/calibrations in date, no active critical alarm, WFI released [Annex 1 4.16, 5.2, 6.12]
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Block start; deviation if bypassed

signatures_required: QA document control: issuance of executed record
Production supervisor: acceptance and pre-start check
Second person (QA where required by SOP): line clearance verification
Person verifying automated gate results (automated equipment under 21 CFR 211.68(c))
special_checks: Only an approved, effective master for that batch size can be instantiated [21 CFR 211.186(a)].

Region rule pack by market. For multi-market batches the strictest rule applies: EU zero-growth APS acceptance (Annex 1 9.46) vs FDA 2004 graded criteria; EU PUPSIT expectation (8.87) vs FDA 'can be performed' (IX.B); EU Grade A-D limits vs FDA ISO 5-8 Table 1.
DEVIATION TRIGGERS: batch started with an expired APS, qualification, requalification or calibration; unqualified person entered; critical alarm open; unreleased WFI used.
Sources: https://health.ec.europa.eu/system/files/2022-08/20220825_gmp-an1_en_0.pdf ; https://www.fda.gov/media/71026/download ; https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-211
time_limits_or_hold_times: APS periodic revalidation ~6 months per line/process/shift; each operator in at least one successful APS every 12 months [Annex 1 9.38]
Cleanroom requalification: A/B ≤6 months, C/D ≤12 months [Annex 1 4.32]
Gowning requalification at least annually [Annex 1 7.4; FDA 2004 V.A]
unit_operations.variant_applicability: All variants. APS and Grade A/B personnel gates apply to aseptic variants (AF-*, AC-*). For TS-* the gate covers Grade C/D status, EM, sterilizer qualification and utilities.

unit_operations.name: Dispensing and weighing (API, excipients, WFI, process gases)
unit_operations.purpose: Dispense released components in the correct quantities with complete traceability and second-person verification. Apply potency and overage calculations.
bmr_records: Per component: material code/name, supplier and supplier lot, internal receiving/control number, QC release status, retest/expiry date, required quantity (calculated), tolerance, gross/tare/net weights, balance ID and daily check result, dispensing room and grade, date/time, dispensed by, verified by [21 CFR 211.101(b)-(d), 211.188(b)(3)-(4), 211.84(a); EU Ch.4 4.20]
Dispensed-container label: component name/code, receiving/control number, weight or measure, and the batch it is dispensed for (product name, strength, lot) [21 CFR 211.101(b)(1)-(4)]

Inputs to the potency-adjusted API calculation (assay as-is or anhydrous, water/solvent content, salt-to-base factor, approved overage) and the calculated quantity. Calculation is independently verified, or performed by validated automated equipment [21 CFR 211.101(a), 211.186(b)(4)-(5), 211.68]
Microbiological/endotoxin status of components liable to objectionable contamination (including WFI and excipients) [21 CFR 211.84(d)(6); FDA 2004 VI.A]
Sterile components for aseptic compounding (sterile API/excipient): sterility and endotoxin CoA, sterilization method, container integrity check at transfer [Annex 1 8.11(ii)]
WFI draw: system and point of use, quantity (load cell or flowmeter), temperature at point of use
Process gas (N2/CO2): identity, supply and point-of-use filter ID
critical_process_parameters: Correct quantity of each component, including potency adjustment and overage
Protection conditions for sensitive materials (light, temperature, inert atmosphere)

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Target ± MBR tolerance (company-defined, e.g. ±0.5% API, ±1-2% excipients; illustrative, not regulatory)
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Re-dispense; out-of-tolerance addition → deviation [21 CFR 211.100(b)]

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Exact match of material, lot, release status and retest date [21 CFR 211.84(a), 211.101(c)(1)]
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Hard block; deviation if overridden

signatures_required: Second-person verifier of release status, weight and container identity [21 CFR 211.101(c)]. One person may suffice where automated equipment under 211.68 performs the weighing
Calculation verifier (second person or validated system check)
special_checks: Sterile powders are weighed and transferred only in Grade A via RTP/alpha-beta port or equivalent validated transfer [Annex 1 4.11, 8.11].
DEVIATION TRIGGERS: out-of-tolerance weight; unreleased or expired lot used; label/identity mismatch; calculation discrepancy.
Sources: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-211 ; https://www.fda.gov/media/71026/download
time_limits_or_hold_times: Maximum hold of dispensed materials before compounding, with storage conditions (company-defined, validated).
unit_operations.variant_applicability: All variants. Sterile-component handling applies to AC-SUSP/EMUL and sterile additions.

unit_operations.name: Primary container preparation: washing and dry-heat depyrogenation (vials/ampoules/cartridges) or RTU nested-container transfer (PFS/RTU)
unit_operations.purpose: Deliver clean, sterile, non-pyrogenic containers to Grade A within validated hold times.
bmr_records: Container code, supplier lot, quantity issued, washer ID and program, WFI final-rinse confirmation (FDA: final rinse water should meet WFI), rinse pressures/temperatures, compressed air (filtered) pressure, number washed, breakage events, start/end time [FDA 2004 VI.B.1; Annex 1 8.2]

Depyrogenation tunnel: ID, program, hot-zone setpoint and actual min/max temperature, cooling-zone temperature, belt speed setpoint/actual (dwell), zone ΔP/airflow profile, container exit temperature, Grade A particle counts in cooling/exit zone, alarms and stops, FD value if calculated, date of last HEPA integrity test (at least biannual) [Annex 1 8.66-8.67; USP <1228.1>]
Batch dry-heat oven (if used): cycle ID, load pattern, temperature/time at coldest position, chamber overpressure, chart/report [Annex 1 8.70; Ph. Eur. 5.1.1]

RTU nested tubs/bags (PFS, RTU vials): supplier lot, sterilization certificate (method/dose/date) and expiry, outer packaging integrity inspection, de-bagging location/grade, surface decontamination record for tub transfer (e-beam dose or VHP cycle ID), number of tubs/nests [Annex 1 8.46-8.48, 8.138]
Time out of tunnel/decontamination to start of filling (sterile-hold clock)
critical_process_parameters: Belt speed / dwell time in sterilizing zone
Airflow/pressure-difference profile correlated with heat distribution and penetration
Washer final rinse quality and pressure
Tub decontamination dose or VHP concentration/time

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Within validated ranges (process validated for ≥3 log10 endotoxin reduction per Annex 1 8.68 / FDA 2004 VI.B.1; USP <1228.1> (2024) uses FD with Tref 250 °C, z 50 °C, and post-process endotoxin NMT 0.1 EU/sample in confirmation studies)
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Tunnel auto-stop and reject containers in the affected window; investigate non-conforming cycle [Annex 1 8.41]

in_process_controls.test: Total particles at tunnel exit / Grade A zone
in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Grade A: ≤3,520/m³ ≥0.5 µm, ≤29/m³ ≥5 µm in operation [Annex 1 Table 5]
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Alarm, containers at risk quarantined, investigation [Annex 1 9.13]

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Validated profile maintaining Grade A protection [Annex 1 8.67]
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Stop, assess heating profile impact, deviation

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Remove the SOP-defined number of containers around the break (USP <1790> 4.x breakage handling)
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Record event and units removed; trend

signatures_required: Supervisor: review of tunnel/oven printout or electronic record
QA: cycle records reviewed at batch disposition
special_checks: EU/US DIFFERENCE: Annex 1 8.68 requires validation to show a minimum 3 log10 endotoxin reduction. USP <1228.1> (official 1 Mar 2024) may accept time-temperature (FD) evidence without a spiked 3-log challenge. Configure per market; strictest applies.
Tunnel parts contacting sterilized components must be sterilized or disinfected. A conveyor must not pass from Grade A/B to a lower grade unless continually sterilized [Annex 1 5.8, 8.67].
DEVIATION TRIGGERS: temperature below minimum or belt speed above maximum; HEPA test overdue; Grade A particle excursion at exit; hold time exceeded; RTU sterilization certificate missing or expired.
Sources: https://health.ec.europa.eu/system/files/2022-08/20220825_gmp-an1_en_0.pdf ; https://doi.org/10.31003/USPNF_M8098_02_01 ; https://www.fda.gov/media/71026/download
time_limits_or_hold_times: Maximum hold between washing, drying and depyrogenation/sterilization [Annex 1 8.18(i)]
Maximum hold of depyrogenated/sterilized containers before and during filling [Annex 1 8.18(ii); FDA 2004 VI.B.1]
Illustrative industry practice (unverified): depyrogenated vials held in Grade A for 24-72 h, or as validated
unit_operations.variant_applicability: AF-VIAL-LIQ, AF-AMP, AF-LYO (tunnel/oven). AF-PFS and RTU presentations use the RTU tub transfer path. TS-*: containers cleaned by a validated process controlling particles, endotoxin and bioburden (Annex 1 8.2); depyrogenation per product/container risk.

unit_operations.name: Closure preparation: stoppers/plungers (washing, siliconization, steam sterilization, drying, or RTU) and caps/seals
unit_operations.purpose: Provide sterile, non-pyrogenic, dry closures (low moisture for lyophilized products) to Grade A within validated hold times.
bmr_records: Closure code, supplier lot, type (ready-to-sterilize or ready-to-use, steam or gamma sterilized), supplier CoA incl. endotoxin/bioburden, quantity issued [21 CFR 211.84, 211.94(c)-(d)]

In-house processing: washer/processor ID, program, WFI final rinse, silicone type/lot and quantity, sterilization cycle ID (unique), load pattern ID, chamber drain temperature trace, exposure time/temperature/pressure, drying phase (vacuum pulses/time), cycle pass/fail, bag/wrap integrity after unloading, sterile-hold expiry [Annex 1 8.44-8.46, 8.56-8.58; FDA 2004 VI.B.1]
Residual moisture of stoppers for lyophilized products (KF result vs limit)
Caps/overseals: type, colour, lot, printed cautionary statement per USP <7>; sterilization record if capping is aseptic [Annex 1 8.27]
critical_process_parameters: Steam sterilization temperature/time/pressure and air removal
Time between washing, drying and sterilizing (bioburden/endotoxin growth risk)

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Within validated parameters; unique cycle ID; record reviewed and approved as part of batch certification [Annex 1 8.41, 8.45]
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Reject load; re-process only per validated procedure; investigate

in_process_controls.test: Load dryness and packaging integrity on unloading
in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Dry, undamaged, integral barrier [Annex 1 8.56-8.57]
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Remove item from manufacturing area, investigate [Annex 1 8.57]

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Product/validation-specific limit (company-defined)
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Additional drying per validated cycle or reject

signatures_required: QA review of sterilization record at release [Annex 1 8.45]
special_checks: Differentiate sterilized from non-sterilized items by label or electronic tracking with product, batch and status [Annex 1 8.44].
Rubber is a poor heat conductor: routine loads must match validated heat-penetration patterns [FDA 2004 VI.B.1, IX.C.1].
DEVIATION TRIGGERS: cycle outside validated parameters; wet or damaged packs; hold time exceeded; missing supplier sterilization evidence for RTU closures.
Sources: https://health.ec.europa.eu/system/files/2022-08/20220825_gmp-an1_en_0.pdf ; https://www.fda.gov/media/71026/download
time_limits_or_hold_times: Washing → drying → sterilization hold minimized and validated [Annex 1 8.18(i); FDA 2004 VI.B.1]
Sterile hold before use in sealed packaging [Annex 1 8.46]
unit_operations.variant_applicability: AF-VIAL-LIQ, AF-LYO (low-moisture stoppers), AF-PFS (plungers/tip caps, usually RTU), TS-* (clean closures; sterility achieved by terminal cycle). Not applicable to fusion-sealed AF-AMP.

unit_operations.name: Equipment/product-path preparation and sterilization; single-use systems; isolator/RABS decontamination; lyophilizer sterilization
unit_operations.purpose: Sterilize every direct and indirect product-contact surface and the barrier environment, with validated, fully recorded cycles and hold times.
bmr_records: CIP: circuit/recipe, detergent concentration, temperatures, times, final-rinse WFI conductivity/TOC
Assembly list of product-contact parts (filling needles, pumps, manifolds, stopper bowl and tracks, filter housings, tubing), part IDs, wrapping, assembled by [Annex 1 5.5]

Autoclave porous/hard-goods load: sterilizer ID, unique cycle ID, program, validated load pattern ID, item list, drain temperature throughout exposure, exposure time/temperature/pressure, equilibration time, pass/fail, BIs/CIs if used, daily air-removal (Bowie-Dick) test result, weekly vacuum leak test status, dryness/integrity check at unloading, sterile-hold expiry [Annex 1 8.38, 8.45, 8.50, 8.56-8.61; FDA 2004 IX.C.1 (batch records document adherence to validated load patterns)]

SIP: system/circuit ID, temperature at condensate drains/cold points, time at or above setpoint, pressure, manual valve manipulations performed, post-SIP positive pressure or sterile vent filter status, vent filter post-use integrity test [Annex 1 8.58, 8.63, 8.88; FDA 2004 IX.C.2]

Single-use systems: item code/lot, supplier certificate of conformance and sterilization proof, expiry, outer packaging/pouch inspection on receipt and before use, connections made (intrinsic sterile connection device type), integrity/pressure test if required [Annex 1 8.129, 8.134, 8.138]

Isolator: VHP (or other sporicide) cycle ID and parameters (concentration, time, temperature, RH, aeration end-point residual), BI/CI results where required, isolator leak test status, glove-port integrity test results at the beginning (and end) of batch/campaign, decontamination hold expiry [Annex 1 4.21(i), 4.22(i), 8.18(iii)]

RABS: sporicidal disinfection record, gloves sterilized before installation and sterilized/bio-decontaminated before each campaign, visual glove check each use, door-opening log [Annex 1 4.21(ii), 4.22(ii)]
Lyophilizer: sterilization (SIP) cycle ID/date, re-sterilization after maintenance/cleaning, sterile hold status, integrity maintained [Annex 1 8.122-8.124]
critical_process_parameters: Sterilization temperature/time/pressure and F0 at slowest-to-heat point
Air removal (porous loads) and condensate drainage

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Within validated ranges. Independent duplex control/monitoring probes must detect non-conforming cycles [Annex 1 8.41, 8.50]
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Reject load / re-sterilize per validated procedure; investigate; items not released to Grade A

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Pass [Annex 1 8.61]
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Sterilizer out of use until repaired and passing

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Within leak-rate specification [Annex 1 8.60]
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Out of use; impact assessment for loads since last pass

in_process_controls.frequency: Minimum at beginning and end of each batch or campaign; visual check each use [Annex 1 4.21(i)]
in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Pressure-decay/leak criterion of the validated tester
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Replace glove. An end-of-batch failure triggers a deviation and batch impact assessment: interventions made through that port, glove prints, EM

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Below validated product-safe level (e.g. ≤1 ppm is common; product-specific, unverified)
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Extend aeration; do not start

signatures_required: Second person (load pattern and item list verification)
QA (approval of sterilization records at batch certification) [Annex 1 8.45]
special_checks: Equipment should normally be sterilized between batches unless alternate intervals are validated [FDA 2004 IX.C].
Unplanned maintenance on sterility-critical equipment needs a recorded sterility impact assessment and approved return to use [Annex 1 5.6-5.7].
Direct and indirect product-contact parts must be sterilized [Annex 1 5.5].

DEVIATION TRIGGERS: failed or non-conforming cycle; overdue Bowie-Dick or leak test; glove integrity failure; sterile/decontamination hold expired; SUS without sterilization proof or with damaged packaging.
Sources: https://health.ec.europa.eu/system/files/2022-08/20220825_gmp-an1_en_0.pdf ; https://www.fda.gov/media/71026/download ; https://doi.org/10.31003/USPNF_M7409_02_01
time_limits_or_hold_times: Dirty-hold and clean-hold before sterilization [Annex 1 8.18(i)]
Sterilized equipment hold before use and during filling/assembly [Annex 1 8.18(ii), 8.46]
Decontaminated isolator/RABS hold before use [Annex 1 8.18(iii)]
Lyophilizer sterile hold, challenged in APS [Annex 1 8.122]
Illustrative industry practice (unverified): sterilized wrapped parts 72 h to 7 days, or as validated
unit_operations.variant_applicability: All aseptic variants. TS-* use cleaned (not necessarily sterilized) filling equipment unless the CCS requires otherwise. Lyophilizer items apply to AF-LYO.

unit_operations.name: Compounding / bulk solution preparation
unit_operations.purpose: Prepare a homogeneous bulk at the correct concentration, pH, density and osmolality with controlled oxygen, bioburden and endotoxin. Start the product time-limit clock.
bmr_records: Vessel ID with clean (and, if required, sterile) status and expiry; agitator ID/speed; load cell ID
T0 = start of product preparation (date/time; e.g. first WFI or first component into vessel, per MBR definition). Starts the product time-limit clock [Annex 1 8.18(iv), 8.36; FDA 2004 VIII]
WFI: initial quantity, point-of-use temperature at addition (product-specific; WFI loop itself e.g. circulated >70 °C), POU/system sample reference [Annex 1 6.10, 6.13]
Each addition: order, material, lot, quantity, time, added by, verified by [21 CFR 211.101(d), 211.188(b)(3)-(4)]
Dissolution/mixing time and visual clarity checks
Nitrogen sparging/overlay: gas source, point-of-use 0.22 µm filter ID, flow/pressure, start/end time, dissolved-oxygen readings [Annex 1 6.18-6.19]
pH measurement(s): meter ID/calibration, value, acid/base adjustment lot, volume added, repeat reading
Final q.s.: target and actual net weight (or volume), temperature at q.s.
Density (g/mL at stated temperature; densitometer ID), osmolality (osmometer ID) [USP <785>], appearance
Bulk samples: assay, pH, density, osmolality, bioburden (pre-filtration, representative of worst case e.g. end of hold), endotoxin; sample IDs and times [Annex 1 8.93, 10.3; FDA 2004 X.C]
Bulk hold: start/end, temperature, N2 blanket, light protection; bulk yield (actual net vs theoretical)
Room and grade: Grade C for solutions to be sterile-filtered (Table 4); Grade D for terminally sterilized products, or Grade C when at high/unusual risk [Annex 1 8.1, Table 3]
critical_process_parameters: Quantity and order of addition of each component
WFI temperature at addition and bulk temperature during mixing
pH adjustment within allowed acid/base volume

in_process_controls.frequency: After dissolution; after each adjustment; final
in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Product/MA-specific range [21 CFR 211.110(a)(5)]
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Adjust within approved limits and re-measure. Adjustment beyond approved limits → deviation [21 CFR 211.100(b)]

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Product-specific; the measured value drives fill-weight targets
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Re-measure; if out of range investigate compounding error; hold

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Product-specific (e.g. near-isotonic ~270-330 mOsm/kg for many IV products; illustrative, unverified) [USP <785>]
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Hold; investigate

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Company release-to-filtration limit (e.g. 98.0-102.0% of target; illustrative)
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Hold. Any correction only per approved procedure with QU approval [21 CFR 211.115]

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Clear, free of visible particles (solutions) [21 CFR 211.110(a)(5)]
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Hold; investigate

in_process_controls.frequency: During/at end of sparge and before filtration
in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Product-specific (e.g. ≤1-2 mg/L; illustrative, unverified)
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Continue sparging within time limits; else deviation

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Alert/action derived from finished-product limit K/M [USP <85>] and input levels
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Investigate. Note: sterilizing filtration and moist heat do not remove endotoxin [FDA 2004 VII]

signatures_required: Second-person verifier for each component addition [21 CFR 211.101(d)]
special_checks: WFI continuous TOC/conductivity monitoring, and at least one representative WFI sample every day of use [Annex 1 6.13, 6.15].

Gases in direct product contact are filtered at point of use by a ≤0.22 µm sterilizing-grade filter. Batch-basis gas filters (e.g. overlay) are integrity-tested and reviewed at release [Annex 1 6.19].
DEVIATION TRIGGERS: wrong order or quantity of addition; pH adjustment beyond allowed range; T0-based limit exceeded; bulk hold temperature excursion; WFI out of specification; IPC failure.

time_limits_or_hold_times: T0 (start of preparation) → sterilizing filtration → end of aseptic filling: product-specific validated maximum [Annex 1 8.18(iv); FDA 2004 VIII; 21 CFR 211.111]
TS products: maximum permissible time between preparation and filling [Annex 1 8.5], and between start of preparation and sterilization [Annex 1 8.36]
Pre-filtration holding time as a validated filtration parameter [Annex 1 8.85(ii)]

Illustrative industry values (unverified; must come from bioburden/endotoxin hold studies): compounding start → end of sterile filtration often ≤8-12 h at room temperature; compounding start → end of filling often ≤24 h (longer only if validated)
unit_operations.variant_applicability: All liquid variants. For AF-LYO the bulk is filterable solution. For AC-SUSP/EMUL see the aseptic compounding step.

unit_operations.name: Aseptic compounding of non-filterable products (suspensions/emulsions) - variant-specific
unit_operations.purpose: Produce a sterile, homogeneous suspension or emulsion from separately sterilized components where final sterilizing filtration is impossible.
bmr_records: Sterilization records of all product-contact equipment; sterile raw materials/intermediates with sterility and endotoxin evidence; aseptic additions (time, operator, Grade A) [Annex 1 8.11(i)-(iii), 8.13]
Homogenizer/microfluidizer ID, pressure, number of passes, temperature, time
Particle size distribution (suspensions) or MDD and PFAT5 (lipid injectable emulsions)
Content uniformity/homogeneity samples at start, middle and end of filling; continuous agitation during filling (speed)
Sterile bulk hold time and conditions
critical_process_parameters: Order and rate of aseptic addition

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Intensity-weighted MDD <500 nm; PFAT5 (volume % of fat in globules >5 µm) ≤0.05% [USP <729>]
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Hold; investigate homogenization; reject if out of specification

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Product specification (MA)
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Hold; investigate

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Product specification
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Investigate agitation; batch impact

special_checks: The APS must cover all additional aseptic steps of non-filterable formulations [Annex 1 9.33(ii)]. FDA 2004 Appendix 3: formulation-stage process simulations at least twice per year.
DEVIATION TRIGGERS: any exposure of sterile materials outside Grade A; homogenizer parameter excursion; hold time exceeded.

time_limits_or_hold_times: Sterile bulk hold before filling [Annex 1 8.18(v)]
Aseptic processing time [Annex 1 8.18(vi)]

unit_operations.name: Sterilizing filtration (including bioburden-reduction prefiltration, PUPSIT and post-use integrity testing)
unit_operations.purpose: Render the bulk sterile by filtration through a validated sterilizing-grade (≤0.22 µm) filter train and prove filter integrity before and after use.
bmr_records: Validated filter train configuration ID (prefilters, serial/redundant sterilizing filters, vent filters) [Annex 1 8.81, 8.91-8.92]

Each filter: manufacturer, catalogue/part no., lot, serial no., pore rating, area; housing/capsule ID; sterilization record (autoclave/SIP cycle ID) or supplier gamma certificate for SUS [Annex 1 8.79, 8.134]
Wetting fluid, flush volume and flush disposal

Pre-use post-sterilization integrity test (PUPSIT): test type (bubble point / diffusive flow / pressure hold / water intrusion), test gas, test pressure, temperature, stabilization time, measured value, specification (validated, correlated to bacterial retention; product-wet or water-wet), pass/fail, number of retests, tester ID/calibration, electronic result file with hash [Annex 1 8.82(vi), 8.87; PDA TR26 Revised 2025]
Pre-filtration bioburden sample ID/time (immediately prior to final sterile filtration; before first filter if redundant) [Annex 1 8.93]

Filtration: start/end time, volume filtered, inlet pressure, differential pressure, flow rate, temperature, total filter contact time, minimum time to filter a known volume [Annex 1 8.85(ii), 8.86; Ph. Eur. 5.1.1 routine control parameters]
Receiving sterile vessel/bag ID, its sterilization record, vent filter ID
Post-use integrity test, performed before removal from housing: same data fields; redundant filter tested if primary fails [Annex 1 8.87, 8.91-8.92]
Critical vent/gas filter post-use integrity test results (product vessel vents, gas overlay filters used per batch) [Annex 1 6.19, 8.88]
Filter disposal confirmation after single batch (or validated campaign duration) [Annex 1 8.94-8.95]
critical_process_parameters: Maximum differential pressure and flow rate
Maximum filtration time / total contact time
Maximum filtered volume per filter area
Integrity-test specification (bubble point minimum or diffusive-flow maximum at test pressure)

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Validated specification correlated to bacterial retention [Annex 1 8.87]. EU: expected unless omission is justified by a documented risk assessment covering filter sterilization, supply chain, packaging, product fouling and prefiltration [Annex 1 8.87(i)-(iii)]. US: 'can be performed prior to processing' [FDA 2004 IX.B]
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Run the validated failure-analysis decision tree (re-wet and retest, more aggressive wetting, lower-surface-tension reference fluid; maximum number of repetitions pre-defined) [PDA TR26 Revised 2025 7.6]. Confirmed failure: replace filter and do not filter. Deviation if procedure not followed

in_process_controls.frequency: After filtration, before removing the filter from its housing
in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Validated specification (product-wet or water-wet) [Annex 1 8.87; FDA 2004 IX.B: should be routinely performed post-use; Ph. Eur. 5.1.1]
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Decision tree as above. A true failure means the batch cannot be released as sterile; reject or re-filter only if validated/registered with QU approval [21 CFR 211.115; PDA TR26 7.5]. Redundant set-up: test the redundant filter and investigate the primary failure [Annex 1 8.92]. Serial validated system: all filters must pass [Annex 1 8.91]

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Validated maxima [Annex 1 8.85-8.86]
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Stop; document and investigate any significant difference from validated parameters [Annex 1 8.86]

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Established limit (FDA 2004 X.C); EU typically NMT 10 CFU/100 mL (EMA 2019 guideline, not verified here; PDA TR90)
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Investigation. Filter-validation challenge margin (≥10^7 CFU/cm² B. diminuta) assessed

signatures_required: Second-person verifier of integrity-test result, or automated transfer from a validated tester with one person checking [21 CFR 211.68(c)]
QA: review of all filter integrity results before release [Annex 1 6.19, 8.124]
special_checks: Final filtration as close to point of fill as possible; connections after the final filter made aseptically in Grade A or by SIP/ISCD [Annex 1 8.14, 8.80, 8.128].
Identical filter (polymer, pore rating) to the validated one [FDA 2004 IX.B].
Integrity-test method by area (PDA TR26 2025 Table 7.1.1-1, approximate): <0.03 m² bubble point; 0.03-1.8 m² bubble point or diffusive flow; >1.8 m² combined.

DEVIATION TRIGGERS: PUPSIT/post-use failure after decision tree; retest count exceeded; filter discarded before test; ΔP/flow/time/volume outside validated limits; wrong filter type; T0 limit exceeded; missing gas/vent filter test.

time_limits_or_hold_times: Pre-filtration holding time [Annex 1 8.85(ii)]
Maximum filtration time / fluid contact time; a single filter not used more than one working day unless validated [Annex 1 8.85(ii), 8.94; FDA 2004 VIII]
Sterile filtrate hold before filling [Annex 1 8.18(v)]
Overall T0 → end of filling [Annex 1 8.18(iv)]
unit_operations.variant_applicability: Sterilizing filtration: AF-VIAL-LIQ, AF-AMP, AF-PFS, AF-LYO. TS-*: bioburden-reduction filtration 'where possible' with a maximum time to filling [Annex 1 8.5]. Not applicable to the final product of AC-SUSP/EMUL (components filtered separately).

unit_operations.name: Aseptic line set-up, gowning/entry and pre-fill checks
unit_operations.purpose: Assemble sterilized equipment and introduce sterile components into Grade A without contamination, with complete EM and intervention coverage from the start of set-up.
bmr_records: Gowning/entry log: person, time in/out, qualification status at entry, sterilized garment lot and within hold time, packaging checked intact, maximum wear time [Annex 1 7.11, 7.15]
Persons present vs maximum permitted number [Annex 1 7.2]
Transfer of each sterilized item into Grade A/B: item ID, sterilization cycle ID, sterile expiry, wrap integrity check, exterior disinfection, approved transfer list [Annex 1 4.12(ii), 8.47-8.48]
Aseptic assembly steps as inherent interventions: start/end times, operators [Annex 1 8.12, 8.16-8.17]
EM from start of set-up: continuous total particle monitoring, continuous viable air monitoring (active air and/or settle plates, with placement/removal times) [Annex 1 9.16, 9.24]
Fill-system set-up: pump/needle configuration, set-up fill weights (units consumed and their disposition), nitrogen overlay connection and filter ID, stopper bowl loaded (lot), line-speed setpoint
Barrier status before start: isolator pressure/decon hold valid, RABS doors closed, UDAF running; critical alarms clear; authorization to start filling
critical_process_parameters: Grade A conditions (UDAF, first air, pressure cascade)
Integrity of sterile packaging at transfer

in_process_controls.frequency: Until n consecutive in-limit results per needle (per MBR)
in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Target ± action limits (see filling step)
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Adjust; set-up units discarded and counted

in_process_controls.test: Particle counter and alarm functional check
in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Counter online, ≥28.3 L/min sampling, alarms active [Annex 1 9.17]
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Do not start

signatures_required: QA or qualified observer for regular observation of aseptic operations [Annex 1 8.19, 9.27]
special_checks: Unwrapping, assembly and filling-line set-up are treated as aseptic processes in Grade A with Grade B background (isolator background per 4.20) [Annex 1 8.12].
Only approved items transferred; unapproved items need pre-approved exception with risk assessment and specific disinfection/monitoring [Annex 1 4.12(ii)].
DEVIATION TRIGGERS: unqualified entrant; expired garment/sterile item; broken sterile barrier; EM not running at set-up; personnel above maximum.
Sources: https://health.ec.europa.eu/system/files/2022-08/20220825_gmp-an1_en_0.pdf
time_limits_or_hold_times: Sterilized item in-use/hold limits [Annex 1 8.18(ii)]
Settle plate exposure ≤4 h per plate [Annex 1 Table 6 note a]
Maximum operator time in cleanroom / gown wear time [Annex 1 7.15, 9.36(ix)]
unit_operations.variant_applicability: Aseptic variants (AF-*, AC-*). TS-* filling set-up follows a clean (non-aseptic) procedure in Grade C.

unit_operations.name: Aseptic filling and closing (vial stoppering, ampoule fusion sealing, PFS filling/plunger placement)
unit_operations.purpose: Fill the exact dose into sterile containers and close them in Grade A. Capture every intervention, stoppage, EM result and IPC needed to demonstrate asepsis.
bmr_records: Filling start/end date-time, line speed setpoint/actual, machine counters (containers in, filled, rejected by reason)
Fill-weight checks: time, needle/pump, gross, tare, net, calculated volume via density, operator or balance-interface ID [21 CFR 211.110(a)]
Inert-gas overlay/headspace oxygen results (if applicable)
Stopper presence/seating verification results; ampoule sealing parameters (gas/oxygen flow, flame settings) and seal checks; PFS plunger placement method, depth/position and bubble-size checks

Intervention log for each event: approved intervention ID/description, category (inherent/corrective), critical (Grade A) yes/no, start and end time, duration, operators, units removed per SOP, extent of line clearance, glove change, glove print sample ID [Annex 1 8.16-8.17, 9.25; FDA 2004 XII; PDA TR22 2025]
Line stoppages: start/end, cause
Non-qualified interventions: QA authorization, risk assessment, deviation number [Annex 1 8.16]

EM during filling: continuous particle data (0.5 and 5 µm) with alarm events; active air sample IDs/times/volumes; settle plate placement/removal; end-of-operation surface/contact plates; personnel monitoring (gloves after critical interventions and at each Grade B exit, gowns) [Annex 1 9.16-9.18, 9.22-9.26]
Glove or gown tears/damage events [PDA PtC No.1 Revised 2023]
Differential-pressure, HVAC, door-interlock and isolator/RABS alarms; any power disruption, however momentary [Annex 1 4.16; FDA 2004 XII]
Sterility samples: IDs and positions (beginning, end, after critical interventions/excursions) [Annex 1 10.6(i); FDA 2004 XI.B]
End of filling: residual bulk, line losses, containers reconciled at filler
critical_process_parameters: Grade A environmental conditions (UDAF velocity guidance 0.36-0.54 m/s at working position, first air, ΔP ≥10 Pa guidance between grades)

in_process_controls.frequency: Start (all needles), then at defined intervals per needle (typically every 15-30 min; illustrative), after every adjustment, intervention or stoppage. Alternatively 100% in-process checkweighing
in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Target = (labeled volume + recommended excess per USP <1151>, e.g. 10 mL label → 0.50 mL mobile / 0.70 mL viscous) × density. Individual units must deliver the labeled volume [USP <697>]. Alert/action limits company-defined (e.g. ±1-2%; illustrative)
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Adjust and re-check; segregate and assess units since last in-limit check; reject out-of-limit units. Action-limit breach → deviation

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: All defective units rejected [Annex 1 8.28; FDA 2004 IV.E]
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Automatic reject. A manual fix is a corrective intervention (log)

in_process_controls.frequency: Continuous for full duration incl. set-up, ≥28.3 L/min
in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Action ≤3,520/m³ (≥0.5 µm) and ≤29/m³ (≥5 µm) in operation; alert levels from qualification/trends [Annex 1 Table 5, 9.9-9.10, 9.16-9.17]. FDA ISO 5: ≤3,520/m³ ≥0.5 µm within ~1 ft of work site [FDA 2004 IV.A]
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Alarm, root-cause investigation, product impact assessment incl. batches produced between monitoring and reporting [Annex 1 9.13]

in_process_controls.frequency: Continuous viable air in Grade A for full duration; gloves after critical interventions and at each Grade B exit; surfaces at end [Annex 1 9.24-9.25]. FDA: gloves daily or with each lot [FDA 2004 V.C]
in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Grade A: any growth → investigation. Grade B action: 10 CFU/m³ air, 5 CFU/4 h settle, 5 CFU/contact plate, 5 CFU/glove. Grade C: 100/50/25. Grade D: 200/100/50 [Annex 1 Table 6]. FDA action levels: ISO 5 1 CFU/m³ and 1 CFU/4 h; ISO 7 10 CFU/m³ and 5 CFU/4 h [FDA 2004 Table 1]
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Species-level ID for Grade A/B isolates [Annex 1 9.31]; investigation completed before release of impacted batches (PDA TR13 2022 5.x); release gate [Annex 1 10.10]

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Product-specific (e.g. ≤2-5% O2; illustrative, unverified), non-destructive laser headspace analysis
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Adjust gassing, segregate units, deviation if action limit

signatures_required: QA: authorization of non-qualified interventions (in advance, exceptional) and review of intervention log [Annex 1 8.16]
Verifier for any manually entered fill weights (unless balance-interfaced)
special_checks: Every intervention must be drawn from the authorized list of qualified inherent and corrective interventions that has been evaluated in APS [Annex 1 8.16, 9.34].
Outer gloves replaced after glove sampling following critical interventions; gowns replaced after gown sampling [Annex 1 9.25]. Gloves not sanitized immediately before sampling [FDA 2004 V.C].
Line clearance rules after defined interventions [FDA 2004 XII]. Open-door RABS interventions logged and followed by disinfection [FDA CP 7356.002A].
Grade A air must not be obstructed; movement slow and controlled [Annex 1 7.18].

DEVIATION TRIGGERS: non-qualified or undocumented intervention; intervention longer than its defined maximum duration; Grade A particle action exceedance; any Grade A viable growth; glove tear during critical operation; fill-weight action limit; ΔP alarm; power interruption; filling-time or aseptic-processing-time limit exceeded; personnel above maximum.
Sources: https://health.ec.europa.eu/system/files/2022-08/20220825_gmp-an1_en_0.pdf ; https://www.fda.gov/media/71026/download ; https://doi.org/10.31003/USPNF_M98730_04_01
time_limits_or_hold_times: Filling time [Annex 1 8.18(vii)]
Aseptic processing time [Annex 1 8.18(vi)]
Sterile bulk hold before/during filling [Annex 1 8.18(v)]
T0 → end of aseptic filling product maximum [Annex 1 8.18(iv)]
Maximum exposure of open containers and maximum intervention durations (company-defined, APS-qualified)
unit_operations.variant_applicability: AF-VIAL-LIQ, AF-AMP (fusion sealing), AF-PFS (nested tub filling, vacuum/vent-tube stoppering), AF-LYO (partial stoppering), AC-SUSP/EMUL. TS-*: filling in Grade C, or Grade A with C background when at unusual risk [Annex 1 8.3-8.4]; aseptic intervention categories not required, but stoppages, fill weights, EM and time limits are still recorded.

unit_operations.name: Lyophilization (Grade A transfer/loading, freeze-drying cycle, in-chamber stoppering, unloading)
unit_operations.purpose: Dry the partially stoppered product under maintained sterility and record the cycle for batch certification.
bmr_records: Lyophilizer ID; sterilization cycle ID and date; re-sterilization after maintenance/cleaning; sterile-hold status. If manually loaded/unloaded without barrier separation, sterilized before each load (Annex 1 8.123, in operation from 25 Aug 2024) [Annex 1 8.122-8.123]
Leak rate / vacuum integrity test at start of every cycle: measured value vs specified maximum [Annex 1 8.124]
Vent/backfill filter: sterilized before each use; integrity test result included in batch certification [Annex 1 8.124]
Trays and vial support rings: sterile, inspected for damage/deformation [Annex 1 8.122, 8.125]
Transfer of partially stoppered vials under Grade A (cart/UDAF/conveyor ID), loading start/end times, operators [Annex 1 8.126(ii)-(iv)]
Loading pattern: shelf map, trays per shelf, vials per tray, product-temperature probe positions [Annex 1 8.126(i)]

Recipe ID/version; setpoints vs actual traces for freezing (shelf temperature, ramps, holds), annealing, primary drying (shelf temperature, chamber pressure by capacitance manometer, Pirani, condenser temperature), secondary drying; product temperatures; end-of-primary-drying determination (Pirani/CM convergence or pressure-rise test); total cycle time
Alarms/events (vacuum loss, refrigeration, power), with operator acknowledgement and impact assessment
Backfill gas (sterile-filtered N2) and stoppering pressure; hydraulic stoppering force; release to atmosphere
Unloading start/end; vials loaded vs unloaded vs broken/fallen; post-unload Grade A handling if stoppering incomplete [Annex 1 8.126(v)]
Cycle report (electronic or printout) reviewed and signed, with audit trail
critical_process_parameters: Product temperature relative to collapse/eutectic temperature

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: ≤ specified maximum permitted air leakage (equipment/validation-specific) [Annex 1 8.124]
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Do not start; repair; re-sterilize; deviation if product already loaded

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Within validated ranges
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Alarm; deviation; product impact assessment (collapse/meltback, moisture)

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Pass [Annex 1 8.124]
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Investigation; batch sterility assurance assessment

in_process_controls.test: Residual moisture (KF), cake appearance, reconstitution time
in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Product specification
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Hold; investigate

special_checks: Lyophilization is an extension of the aseptic process; all control measures per CCS [Annex 1 8.121].

The APS must represent transport, loading, a representative chamber dwell, unloading and sealing. It uses air (not N2) to break vacuum, the maximum sterilization-to-use interval, the maximum filtration-to-lyo time and the largest number of trays [Annex 1 9.33(vi)-(vii)].
DEVIATION TRIGGERS: leak test failure; unsterilized or expired lyophilizer; partially stoppered vials outside Grade A; cycle parameter excursion; vent filter failure; vial count mismatch.
Sources: https://health.ec.europa.eu/system/files/2022-08/20220825_gmp-an1_en_0.pdf ; https://www.fda.gov/media/71026/download
time_limits_or_hold_times: Maximum time from filling to loading, and maximum loading duration with chamber open (worst case in APS) [Annex 1 9.33(vii)]
Lyophilizer sterile hold before use [Annex 1 8.122]
Maximum hold of stoppered, uncapped vials before capping (validated)

unit_operations.name: Capping / crimping
unit_operations.purpose: Secure the closure with an overseal without compromising the container before crimping. Reject units with missing or displaced stoppers before capping.
bmr_records: Capping machine ID; mode: aseptic (sterilized caps in Grade A) or clean process outside the aseptic core with Grade A air supply in ≥Grade D background [Annex 1 8.27]

Cap/seal type, colour, lot; cap sterilization record if aseptic; verification of ferrule/cap cautionary statement and colour per product labeling (USP <7>: only cautionary statements on the top surface; black closures only for Potassium Chloride Injection Concentrate)
Stopper presence/height detection system status and challenge results; count of units rejected before capping [Annex 1 8.28]
Crimp settings (force/pressure, head height); crimp quality check results (visual/rotation/torque or residual seal force)
Manual interventions at the capping station; local extraction running [Annex 1 8.26, 8.29]
Counts in / capped / rejected
critical_process_parameters: Grade A air supply protection until crimped

in_process_controls.frequency: Start and end of run and at defined intervals (company-defined)
in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Challenge units (raised/missing stopper) are 100% rejected [Annex 1 8.28]
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Stop; repair; re-inspect or re-challenge units processed since last successful challenge; deviation

in_process_controls.test: Crimp quality (visual, cap rotation/torque or RSF)
in_process_controls.frequency: Start and periodically per head (e.g. hourly; illustrative)
in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Validated crimp range (company-defined)
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Adjust; segregate units since last passing check; CCI assessment

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Matches master record
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Stop; segregate

special_checks: Manual capping must be in Grade A with B background or in an isolator [Annex 1 8.27].
FDA: local protection until crimping; on-line detection of improperly seated stoppers [FDA 2004 IV.E].
DEVIATION TRIGGERS: loss of Grade A air supply; failed detector challenge; wrong cap; stoppered-uncapped hold exceeded.
Sources: https://health.ec.europa.eu/system/files/2022-08/20220825_gmp-an1_en_0.pdf ; https://www.fda.gov/media/71026/download
time_limits_or_hold_times: Maximum time stoppered vials may wait before crimping (validated)
unit_operations.variant_applicability: AF-VIAL-LIQ, AF-LYO, vials in TS-SVP. Not applicable to ampoules, PFS or bags.

unit_operations.name: Terminal moist-heat sterilization of filled containers
unit_operations.purpose: Achieve SAL ≤10^-6 in the final sealed container by a validated, controlled cycle with full load traceability.
bmr_records: Load/sub-batch ID, number of units per load, validated loading pattern ID (within min/max load), container type. Only a single container size and single product lot per load [USP <1229.2>; Annex 1 8.38]
Pre-sterilization bioburden sample (each batch; worst-case filled units; spore resistance screening for BB/BI cycles) [Annex 1 10.3-10.4; USP <1229.2>]
Time from start of preparation / end of filling to start of sterilization [Annex 1 8.5, 8.36]

Sterilizer ID, unique cycle ID, program; independent duplex control and monitoring probes; reference/load probe positions (in-container for ≥100 mL containers mapped for cold spots) [Annex 1 8.50-8.52; USP <1229.2>]
Temperature, pressure (incl. air overpressure) and time traces; equilibration and exposure time; F0 per monitored position (min/max); heating/cooling rates [Annex 1 8.59, 8.62]
Cooling medium sterilized (spray/cooling water) [Annex 1 8.53]
Load monitor or BI/CI results where required (parametric release) [FDA 2010 parametric release guidance; Annex 1 8.54, Annex 17]
Periodic tests status (weekly leak test if vacuum phase) [Annex 1 8.60]
Cycle pass/fail, alarms, chart/report reviewed and signed; unloading inspection (deformation, leakers, counts); sterilized/unsterilized segregation labels or electronic status [Annex 1 8.44-8.45]
critical_process_parameters: Exposure temperature and time, or delivered F0 at slowest-heating location (minimum and maximum)
Pre-sterilization bioburden (population and resistance) for BB/BI or bioburden-based cycles

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Ph. Eur. 5.1.1: reference cycle 15 min at 121 °C; minimum acceptable temperature 110 °C; minimum F0 ≥8 min in slowest-to-heat position. Overkill cycles are commonly higher (≥12-15 min; illustrative). A maximum F0 is also set for product degradation
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Cycle fail: load quarantined, investigation [Annex 1 8.41]. Re-sterilization only if validated and approved (reprocessing needs QU approval) [21 CFR 211.115]

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Validated band (e.g. 121-124 °C; illustrative)
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: As above

in_process_controls.frequency: Each batch (and each load where required)
in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Validated maximum; organisms identified and their resistance assessed where relevant [Annex 1 10.4]
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Investigation; PNSU re-evaluation

special_checks: Sub-batches (loads) each need their own sterility test samples from worst-case (coolest) locations [Annex 1 10.6(ii) and note].
Parametric release (if authorized): sterility test replaced by acceptance of critical parameters plus a load monitor in each load [FDA 2010 guidance; CPG 460.800; USP <1222>; EU Annex 17].

DEVIATION TRIGGERS: F0/temperature/time below minimum or above maximum; probe disagreement; load pattern not validated; mixed lots in one load; time-to-sterilization exceeded; cooling water not sterile; unit count mismatch; leakers.

time_limits_or_hold_times: Maximum time preparation → filling → start of sterilization [Annex 1 8.5, 8.36]
Illustrative industry values (unverified): end of filling → start of sterilization often ≤8-12 h
unit_operations.variant_applicability: TS-MH-SVP, TS-MH-LVP. Optional post-aseptic terminal heat treatment for aseptic products [Annex 1 8.34, glossary].

unit_operations.name: 100% visual inspection (manual / semi-automated / automated) and AQL acceptance sampling
unit_operations.purpose: Remove every container with visible particulates or other defects and prove batch quality by statistically based acceptance sampling and trending.
bmr_records: Inspection method (MVI/SAI/AVI), booth/machine ID, AVI recipe/version [Annex 1 8.31-8.32]
Light intensity measured at inspection point (2,000-3,750 lux for clear glass; higher for amber/plastic, e.g. 8,000-10,000 lux), black and white backgrounds [USP <790>; USP <1790>; Ph. Eur. 2.9.20]
Inspector IDs with qualification status (at least annual, including eyesight/visual acuity; defect-library test set) [Annex 1 8.31; USP <1790> 7.8-7.9]
Inspection time/rate (reference 5 s per background = ~10 s per container), documented breaks (e.g. at least hourly) [USP <790>; USP <1790>]
AVI challenge-set results before start-up, at regular intervals and at end [Annex 1 8.32]

Units received; units accepted; rejects by defect category (critical/major/minor) and defect type code from the defect library (e.g. glass/fiber/other particle, crack, missing stopper/cap, crimp, fill level, cake defect, cosmetic); per-inspector counts [Annex 1 8.30, 8.33]
Second-stage inspection or false-reject review (if procedural), reinspection records (QA approval, reason, count) [USP <1790> 3.3]

AQL sampling: plan (ANSI/ASQ Z1.4 or ISO 2859-1, General Inspection Level II, single sampling, normal), lot size, code letter, sample size, AQL per category, accept/reject numbers, defects found, inspector [USP <790>; USP <1790> 3.2]

Supplemental destructive inspection for limited-visibility products (lyophilized, amber, suspensions): sample size (e.g. S-3/S-4 plans, n=20, Ac 0 for 0.65% AQL for lots 200-10,000), results [USP <790>; USP <1790> Table 2]
Reject rates vs alert/action limits per category
critical_process_parameters: AVI sensitivity settings (validated to be equal to or better than manual inspection)

in_process_controls.frequency: Start of each session/shift and periodically
in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: 2,000-3,750 lux (clear glass) [USP <790>; Ph. Eur. 2.9.20]
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Stop; correct; re-inspect units since last passing check

in_process_controls.frequency: Before start-up, at regular intervals, end [Annex 1 8.32]
in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: All reject-zone standards (≥70% PoD) rejected; false reject within limit
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Stop; re-inspect units since last successful challenge; deviation

in_process_controls.frequency: End of 100% inspection (and interim for long runs)
in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Alert/action limits from historical data per category/type [Annex 1 8.30; USP <1790> 3.1]
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Investigation; possible reinspection per approved procedure; market impact assessment for adverse trends [Annex 1 8.33]

in_process_controls.frequency: After each 100% inspection (and after any reinspection, tightened)
in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Visible particulates: AQL 0.65% (Z1.4 GIL II, normal, single) [USP <790>]. Typical AQL ranges: critical 0.010-0.10% (accept number usually 0), major 0.10-0.65%, minor 1.0-4.0%; sample size chosen for the most critical category [USP <1790> Table 1]
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Investigation. Any critical defect found after 100% inspection triggers investigation of the inspection process [Annex 1 8.30]. Reinspection only if the inspection process is shown capable, limited in number, with tightened sampling [USP <1790> 3.2-3.3]

special_checks: Every container showing visible particulates must be rejected [USP <1>].
Defect library maintained and used for training [Annex 1 8.30].

DEVIATION TRIGGERS: unqualified inspector; lux out of range; AVI challenge failure; reject rate above action limit; AQL failure; critical defect found in AQL; unreconciled counts; reinspection without QA approval.
Sources: https://health.ec.europa.eu/system/files/2022-08/20220825_gmp-an1_en_0.pdf ; https://doi.org/10.31003/USPNF_M7197_01_01 ; https://doi.org/10.31003/USPNF_M7198_07_01
time_limits_or_hold_times: Hold of unlabeled (bright stock) units under identification controls [21 CFR 211.130(b)]
Cumulative time out of refrigeration for cold-chain products (product-specific)
unit_operations.variant_applicability: All variants (all parenteral containers must be inspected individually) [Annex 1 8.30]. Supplemental destructive testing is mainly for AF-LYO, amber containers and suspensions/emulsions.

unit_operations.name: Container closure integrity (CCI) testing
unit_operations.purpose: Confirm each fusion-sealed container, or a validated sample of other closures, is integral. Visual inspection alone is not an integrity test.
bmr_records: Container/closure type; CCI method (deterministic preferred: vacuum decay, HVLD, laser headspace analysis, helium leak; probabilistic: dye/microbial ingress); instrument ID and calibration [USP <1207>, <1207.1>, <1207.2>]
Positive control (calibrated leak / laser-drilled defect) and negative control results at start and end of run

Sampling plan: 100% for glass ampoules, BFS units and fusion-closed containers ≤100 mL. Reduced sampling for fusion-closed >100 mL only if justified. Scientifically justified sampling for other closure types [Annex 1 8.22-8.23]
Per-unit or per-sample results, leakers identified, dispositions
Vacuum-sealed containers: maintenance-of-vacuum test after a pre-determined period, before certification [Annex 1 8.24]
critical_process_parameters: Test sensitivity vs maximum allowable leakage limit (e.g. <6×10^-6 mbar·L/s helium for rigid containers per USP <1207>)
Test parameters (vacuum level, voltage, test time)

in_process_controls.frequency: Start and end of each run/shift
in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Detects defect at method LOD; no false rejects on negatives
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Invalidate run; retest units since last passing control

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Pass; zero leakers in sampled plan (company-defined)
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Investigation; escalate to 100% testing; batch rejection if systemic

special_checks: Visual inspection is not an acceptable integrity test [Annex 1 8.22].
Transport stresses (decompression, temperature) considered in CCI validation [Annex 1 8.25].
DEVIATION TRIGGERS: control failure; any leaker in sample; untested fused units.
Sources: https://health.ec.europa.eu/system/files/2022-08/20220825_gmp-an1_en_0.pdf ; https://doi.org/10.31003/USPNF_M99926_01_01
time_limits_or_hold_times: For vacuum-sealed containers: pre-determined interval before vacuum-maintenance test [Annex 1 8.24]
unit_operations.variant_applicability: AF-AMP and fusion-sealed TS-MH-LVP/BFS: 100%. Vials/PFS: sampling or in-line 100% where implemented. AF-LYO under partial vacuum: vacuum maintenance.

unit_operations.name: QC sampling for release (sterility, endotoxin, particulate, content) and reserve/retention samples
unit_operations.purpose: Take representative and worst-case samples tied to process events, in pharmacopoeial quantities.
bmr_records: Sample plan version; each sample ID, type, quantity, time and process position (beginning/middle/end of fill, after critical interventions or excursions, each lyo load, worst-case load positions, each TS sub-batch) [Annex 1 10.6; FDA 2004 XI.B]

Sterility sample count per USP <71> Table 3 (parenterals: ≤100 containers → 10% or 4, whichever greater; 101-500 → 10; >500 → 2% or 20, whichever less; LVP → 2% or 10, whichever less; double the number if contents are insufficient for both media) and quantity per medium per Table 2 (<1 mL whole contents; 1-40 mL half the contents, not less than 1 mL; >40-100 mL 20 mL; >100 mL 10%, not less than 20 mL)
Endotoxin samples (limit = K/M; K = 5 EU/kg, 0.2 EU/kg intrathecal) [USP <85>]
Subvisible particulate samples (LO limits ≤100 mL: ≤6,000 ≥10 µm and ≤600 ≥25 µm per container; >100 mL: ≤25/mL and ≤3/mL) [USP <788>]; for therapeutic proteins USP <787>
Container content / extractable volume samples [USP <697>; Ph. Eur. 2.9.17]
Reserve samples: ≥2× quantity for all tests except sterility and pyrogen, retained 1 year after expiry, stored per labeling [21 CFR 211.170(b)]
Chain of custody; external surface decontamination of sterility samples must not affect the test [Annex 1 10.8]
critical_process_parameters: Representativeness and worst-case coverage of samples

in_process_controls.frequency: At each triggering event and at batch end
in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: All event-driven samples present (start/end/interventions/loads/sub-batches) [Annex 1 10.6]
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Block batch completion; deviation

special_checks: Sterility test is the last in a series of controls and cannot make a non-compliant process acceptable [Annex 1 10.5]. Sampling statistics: USP-based plan detects 10% contamination ~9 times in 10 [FDA 2004 XI.B].
Short shelf-life products may be released before a sterility result per risk-based controls [Annex 1 10.7; 21 CFR 211.165(a) radiopharmaceuticals].
DEVIATION TRIGGERS: missing event-driven samples; insufficient quantity; broken chain of custody.
Sources: https://doi.org/10.31003/USPNF_M98810_01_01 ; https://doi.org/10.31003/USPNF_M98830_02_01 ; https://doi.org/10.31003/USPNF_M99586_02_01
time_limits_or_hold_times: Sample storage/transport conditions and time to test (method validation)

unit_operations.name: Labeling and secondary packaging (Batch Packaging Record) incl. serialization, aggregation, device assembly and cold chain
unit_operations.purpose: Label and pack inspected units correctly with full reconciliation, verified coding and serialization, and controlled temperature exposure.
bmr_records: Packaging order, packaging master version, line ID, bulk (inspected) lot and finished lot linkage [EU Ch.4 4.21; 21 CFR 211.130(c)]
Line clearance before start and after end: checklist, performer, verifier [21 CFR 211.130(e); EU Ch.5]
Printed materials issued: item code, lot, artwork version, quantity; examination for identity and conformity [21 CFR 211.122, 211.125(b), 211.130(d)]
Printed specimens of labels, cartons and leaflets with batch/expiry overprint attached [21 CFR 211.188(b)(8); EU Ch.4 4.21]
Coding verification (batch, expiry) at start, at defined intervals and at end; printer monitoring [21 CFR 211.122(h)]
Vision/barcode checks: linear barcode with NDC on unit label for US Rx products [21 CFR 201.25]; 2D DataMatrix grading [EU 2016/161 Art. 5-6, 14]

Serialization: product code (GTIN/NDC), serial numbers commissioned, rejected/decommissioned, sampled; aggregation hierarchy; upload to EU repositories before release [EU 2016/161 Art. 4, 15, 33]; US product identifier = NDC-based SNI with serial ≤20 characters, lot, expiry, human-readable and machine-readable [21 U.S.C. 360eee(14),(20)]
Anti-tampering device applied and verified (EU) [EU 2016/161 Art. 3(b)]
PFS/cartridges: plunger rod insertion, backstop, needle-safety/autoinjector assembly checks (combination product: 21 CFR Part 4)
Cold chain: per tray/lot time-out-of-refrigeration start/stop and cumulative total vs limit
Counts: units received from inspection, packed, samples, rejected, destroyed; label reconciliation; destruction of batch-coded excess [21 CFR 211.125(c)-(d)]
Finished-product labeling examination: representative sample, results recorded [21 CFR 211.134, 211.188(b)(13)]

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: No previous product, labels or documents [21 CFR 211.130(e)]
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Block start

in_process_controls.frequency: Start, periodic (e.g. each reel change / 30-60 min; illustrative), end
in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Matches batch record [21 CFR 211.122(h)]
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Stop; segregate since last good check; deviation

in_process_controls.test: Vision system challenge (OCR/OCV, barcode, missing leaflet)
in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: All challenge defects rejected [EU Ch.5 5.57-5.58]
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Stop; re-verify units

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Readable, correct, unique serials; grading meets EU Art. 6 parameters
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Reject/decommission; investigate duplicates

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Issued = used + destroyed + returned, within narrow preset limits based on history. Waived for cut/roll labeling with 100% electronic verification [21 CFR 211.125(c), 211.122(g)(2)]
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Investigation per 211.192 before release

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Product-specific cumulative limit (stability-supported)
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Deviation; stability impact assessment

signatures_required: Verifier (second person for hand-applied labels) [21 CFR 211.122(g)(3)]
QA (line clearance approval per SOP; BPR review)
special_checks: USP <7> ferrule/cap rules: only cautionary statements on the top (circular) surface; neuromuscular blockers must carry a paralyzing-agent warning on ferrule and cap; black closure only for Potassium Chloride Injection Concentrate. Verified only against a translated USP 44 copy; confirm against current USP.
Unused batch-coded materials destroyed and recorded [21 CFR 211.125(d)].
