time_limits_or_hold_times: Cumulative time out of refrigeration (product-specific)
Serialization data retention: records of UI operations kept ≥1 year after expiry or 5 years after release, whichever is longer [EU 2016/161 Art. 15]
unit_operations.variant_applicability: All variants (market-specific serialization and labeling rules).

unit_operations.name: Batch record review, sterility-assurance release gate and QU release / QP certification
unit_operations.purpose: Holistic review of production, environmental, support-system and QC data before disposition.
bmr_records: Completion check: all steps executed and signed, no open entries [21 CFR 211.188, 211.192]
Deviations/investigations closed, including scope extension to other batches and products [21 CFR 211.192; Annex 1 3.2]
EM and trend data reviewed for the batch window (viable and non-viable, personnel), incubation complete, species IDs [Annex 1 9.3, 10.10; FDA 2004 XII; FDA CP 7356.002A]
Intervention log reviewed, including any non-qualified intervention [Annex 1 8.16; CP 7356.002A]
APS coverage confirmed for line/shift/process [Annex 1 9.38]
All sterilization/depyrogenation/decontamination records approved [Annex 1 8.45]
All filter integrity results (product, vent, gas, lyophilizer) reviewed [Annex 1 6.19, 8.87, 8.124]
Bioburden results considered [Annex 1 10.3]
Support-system data (HVAC/HEPA, WFI, steam generator) and batch alarm report reviewed [FDA 2004 XII]
Time-limit compliance summary; yields and reconciliations within limits [21 CFR 211.103, 211.186(b)(7)]
QC results (sterility or parametric-release criteria, endotoxin, particulate, visual inspection AQL, CCI, assay) and CoA
Packaging record, label reconciliation and serialization upload confirmation
Disposition: QU approval [21 CFR 211.22, 211.192]; EU QP certification [EU Annex 16] with confirmation that release persons had access to all sterility information [Annex 1 3.1(vii)]

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: All sterility-assurance gates green [Annex 1 3.2, 8.45, 10.3, 10.10; FDA 2004 XII]
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Release blocked; open items routed to owners

special_checks: The eBMR must show that the holistic review of EM/support systems was done before release [FDA CP 7356.002A].
DEVIATION TRIGGERS: any gate not met; late EM result after release (→ recall assessment).
Sources: https://health.ec.europa.eu/system/files/2022-08/20220825_gmp-an1_en_0.pdf ; https://www.fda.gov/media/71026/download ; https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-211
time_limits_or_hold_times: Sterility test incubation ≥14 days before result [USP <71>]

unit_operations.name: Aseptic Process Simulation (media fill) batch record - special record type
unit_operations.purpose: Periodically verify aseptic process capability. The APS result feeds the line, shift and operator qualification gates and the impact analysis for commercial batches.
bmr_records: APS protocol ID, worst-case design rationale (container size, line speed, maximum duration, personnel, hold times, interventions and frequencies, shift change, campaign start/end) [Annex 1 9.33-9.36; FDA 2004 IX.A.1]
Media (e.g. soybean-casein digest), lot, growth promotion; media filtration/sterilization records and filter integrity
Inert gas replaced by air unless anaerobic simulation intended [Annex 1 9.33(iii), 9.36(v)]
Every intervention (inherent/corrective), type, time, duration, operators, box/tray number; stoppages [Annex 1 9.47; PDA TR22 Revised 2025 5.3]
EM throughout the run as for routine production [Annex 1 9.36(xi)]
Units filled; units removed per SOP-defined interventions (never more than in production); set-up units incubated separately [Annex 1 9.41; FDA 2004 IX.A.8]
Reconciliation: rejected at filling (by category), incubated, QC samples, pre-incubation inspection counts, 7-day and 14-day inspection counts (must match) [PDA TR22 2025; Annex 1 9.47]
Incubation: ≥14 days; FDA 20-35 °C, ±2.5 °C of target; if two temperatures, ≥7 days at each, lower first [FDA 2004 IX.A.8]; conditions scientifically justified [Annex 1 9.44]
Inspection by trained, qualified personnel; positive controls [Annex 1 9.45]
Result and participants list (updates operator APS qualification)
critical_process_parameters: Representativeness of worst-case conditions and interventions
Media fill volume sufficient to contact all surfaces

in_process_controls.frequency: At each stage and after incubation
in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Target 100% accountability [PDA TR22 2025]
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Investigation of APS validity

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: EU: target zero; any contaminated unit = failed APS [Annex 1 9.46]. FDA 2004: <5,000 units: 0 (1 → revalidation after investigation); 5,000-10,000: 1 → investigation, consider repeat; 2 → revalidation; >10,000: 1 → investigation; 2 → revalidation
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Investigation; ≥3 consecutive successful repeat APS; review of all batches since last successful APS; quarantine products made on the line after the failure; operator restrictions; resume only after successful revalidation [Annex 1 9.46]

special_checks: Impact scope is not limited to the line. Example: a failure attributed to a lyophilizer impacts all products processed in that unit regardless of fill line; intermittent equipment faults may require review of all batches within expiry [PDA TR22 Revised 2025 section 9-10].
An APS may be aborted only where procedures would require commercial lots to be handled equally [Annex 1 9.48].
Sources: https://health.ec.europa.eu/system/files/2022-08/20220825_gmp-an1_en_0.pdf ; https://www.fda.gov/media/71026/download ; PDA TR22 (Revised 2025) https://www.pda.org
time_limits_or_hold_times: Periodic APS ~6 months per line/process/shift; initial 3 consecutive; each operator yearly [Annex 1 9.38]; manual aseptic processes: each operator 3 initial, then 1 per ~6 months [Annex 1 9.39]

batch_level_records: Header/identity: product, strength, dosage form, container-closure, nominal fill, batch number, batch size (volume/mass and theoretical units), master record ID/version, market(s), site/line/rooms (grade, barrier type), manufacturing and expiry dates with the shelf-life start rule [21 CFR 211.186, 211.188; EU Ch.4 4.17/4.20].

Material genealogy: API and excipient lots, WFI system and POU samples, process gases, primary packaging lots (vials/ampoules/syringe tubs/stoppers/plungers/seals), filters (lot and serial), SUS assemblies, disinfectant lots, media lots, printed materials [21 CFR 211.188(b)(3)].
Equipment and room register with clean, sterile and calibration status at time of use; sterilizer, tunnel, lyophilizer and isolator cycle IDs linked [21 CFR 211.182, 211.188(b)(2); Annex 1 8.45].

Personnel register: everyone who entered Grade A/B or performed or verified steps, with gowning qualification, APS participation and training status at time of action [Annex 1 7.4-7.6; 21 CFR 211.188(b)(11)].

Time-limit ledger: each clock (T0 compounding → filtration → end of fill; sterile holds; exposure; filling time; lyo loading; time to sterilization; TOR) with start, end, limit and status [Annex 1 8.18, 8.5, 8.36; 21 CFR 211.111].
Intervention and stoppage log (inherent/corrective, critical, non-qualified with QA authorization) [Annex 1 8.16-8.17; FDA 2004 XII].
EM summary for the batch window: continuous Grade A particles (0.5 and 5 µm) with alarms; viable air/settle/contact/glove/gown results; excursions, investigations, species IDs [Annex 1 9.x, 10.10].
Alarm and event log: ΔP, HVAC, door interlocks, isolator pressure/glove breaches, equipment alarms, power disruptions [Annex 1 4.16, 5.2; FDA 2004 XII].
Sterilization, depyrogenation, decontamination and SIP records, each with unique cycle ID, pass/fail, approval [Annex 1 8.45].
Filter integrity summary: pre-use/PUPSIT and post-use results for every sterilizing, vent and gas filter [Annex 1 6.19, 8.87-8.88, 8.124].
Utilities summary: WFI TOC/conductivity trends, micro/endotoxin results, clean steam quality, process gas monitoring [Annex 1 6.x; FDA 2004 XII].
IPC summary: pH, density, osmolality, DO/headspace O2, fill weights (SPC), bioburden, bulk endotoxin, lyo moisture, crimp checks.
Yield and reconciliation statements at each stage (bulk, fill, lyo, cap, inspection, packaging, labels, serial numbers) [21 CFR 211.103, 211.188(b)(7); EU Ch.4 4.20/4.21].
Visual inspection summary (100% results by category, AQL results, reinspection) and CCI summary [Annex 1 8.22-8.33].
Sample register (sterility by event/position, endotoxin, particulate, content, reserve/retention, EM samples) [Annex 1 10.6; 21 CFR 211.170].
Links to deviations, investigations (with scope to other batches), CAPA and change controls [21 CFR 211.192; Annex 1 3.2].
Labeling specimens, coding verification and serialization/aggregation reports with repository upload confirmation [21 CFR 211.188(b)(8); EU 2016/161 Art. 15, 33].
APS coverage statement (IDs of the last successful APS for line/process/shift) and CCS references for key controls [Annex 1 2.3-2.6, 9.38].
QC results/CoA, QU disposition [21 CFR 211.192] and EU QP certification [EU Annex 16].
Complete audit trail and e-signature manifestations (printed name, date/time, meaning) for all GMP entries [21 CFR Part 11; EU Annex 11 (2011; July 2025 draft pending)].
yield_and_reconciliation_rules: Bulk yield (%) = actual net bulk (kg or L at q.s.) / theoretical bulk × 100. Master sets min/max; outside limits → investigation before proceeding [21 CFR 211.103, 211.186(b)(7), 211.192].

Filling yield (%) = units filled and accepted at filler / theoretical units × 100. Theoretical units come from available bulk and target fill volume (see calculations). Outside limits → investigation.

Filler unit accountability: containers issued to line = units passed to next step + filler rejects by reason (weight, missing stopper, broken) + set-up/adjustment units + destructive IPC units + samples + broken/lost + unused returned. Unexplained difference must be zero or within a small count tolerance justified in the master; otherwise deviation.
Units removed during interventions must match the numbers the SOP specifies for that intervention type (also for APS) [FDA 2004 IX.A.8; Annex 1 9.41].
Lyophilization: vials loaded = vials unloaded + broken/fallen (recorded with shelf position) + removed samples.
Capping: units in = capped units + rejects (missing/displaced stopper, crimp rejects).
Terminal sterilization: units per load reconciled in = out (+ leakers/damaged) for every load/sub-batch.

Visual inspection: units received = accepted + rejects per category/type + AQL samples (returned or destroyed) + QC samples + destroyed. Reject rates compared with alert/action limits per category; exceedance → investigation [Annex 1 8.30, 8.33; USP <1790> 3.1].

Packaging: units received from inspection = packed + samples + rejected + destroyed. Printed components: issued = used + destroyed + returned, within narrow preset limits based on historical data; discrepancies investigated per 211.192 [21 CFR 211.125(c)]. EU: reconciliation may be omitted only with robust, justified electronic controls [EU Ch.4 4.21(h)]. Roll/cut labeling with 100% electronic verification waives label reconciliation [21 CFR 211.125(c), 211.122(g)(2)].
Serial numbers: commissioned = packed/aggregated + decommissioned (destroyed/sampled/rejected) + unused/returned to pool. Must reconcile before upload/release [EU 2016/161 Art. 15, 33].
Overall batch yield (%) = finished packed units / theoretical units × 100, with master min/max; any value outside limits → investigation extending to other batches [21 CFR 211.192].

APS reconciliation: filled = rejected at filling (categorized) + non-incubated QC samples + incubated units. Incubated count equal at receipt, 7-day and 14-day inspection. Target 100% accountability [PDA TR22 Revised 2025; Annex 1 9.47].

Reprocessing (e.g. re-filtration) or reinspection only per approved procedure with QU approval, recorded as a separate step with its own yield [21 CFR 211.115; USP <1790> 3.3]. For sterile products the default configuration should be 'reprocessing disabled' unless validated and registered.

calculations.name: Potency-adjusted API quantity
calculations.formula: m_API = (C_label × V_batch) × (100 / Assay_as_is%) × (MW_salt / MW_base) × (1 + overage%/100). If assay is on anhydrous basis: divide additionally by (1 − water%/100).
calculations.notes: C_label = labeled concentration of active moiety (e.g. mg/mL). The overage must be stated and justified in the master [21 CFR 211.101(a), 211.186(b)(5)]. Calculation verified by a second person or a validated system [21 CFR 211.103 by analogy, 211.68].

calculations.name: Mass-volume conversion via density
calculations.formula: V = m / ρ ; m = V × ρ (ρ in g/mL at the stated measurement temperature)
calculations.notes: Measured bulk density at the final q.s. drives fill-weight targets. Use the same temperature basis as the density specification.

calculations.name: Target fill volume and fill weight
calculations.formula: V_target = V_label + V_excess ; W_net_target = V_target × ρ ; W_gross_target = W_net_target + tare_container(+closure if weighed stoppered). Alert/action limits: W_net_target × (1 ± a%) and (1 ± b%), with a < b (company-defined).
calculations.notes: Recommended excess per USP <1151> (mobile / viscous): 0.5 mL: 0.10/0.12; 1.0 mL: 0.10/0.15; 2.0 mL: 0.15/0.25; 5.0 mL: 0.30/0.50; 10.0 mL: 0.50/0.70; 20.0 mL: 0.60/0.90; 30.0 mL: 0.80/1.20; ≥50 mL: 2%/3%. Checked only against a translated USP 44 copy; re-check against current USP. Container content testing per USP <697> / Ph. Eur. 2.9.17. Example: 10 mL label, mobile, ρ = 1.012 g/mL → 10.50 mL → 10.626 g net.

calculations.name: Theoretical number of units
calculations.formula: N_theo = floor( (V_bulk_net − V_holdup_filters_lines − V_QC_bulk_samples − V_planned_setup_purge) / V_target )
calculations.notes: All deductions are fixed in the master; alternatively the master states batch size in units. Example: (105.0 − 2.0 − 0.3 − 0.2) L / 0.0105 L = 9,761 units.

calculations.name: Stage yield (%)
calculations.formula: Yield% = (Actual output at stage / Theoretical output at stage) × 100
calculations.notes: Computed at each appropriate phase and verified [21 CFR 211.103]. Master holds min/max percentages beyond which a 211.192 investigation is required [211.186(b)(7)].

calculations.name: Unit reconciliation / accountability (%)
calculations.formula: Accountability% = (Accepted + Σ Rejects_by_reason + Samples(QC, IPC destructive, AQL destroyed, retention) + Broken/Destroyed + Returned) / Units_in × 100 ; Unexplained = Units_in − (numerator sum)
calculations.notes: Applied at filler, lyo, capping, TS load, inspection and packaging. Target 100% with zero or justified count tolerance.

calculations.name: Label/printed-component reconciliation
calculations.formula: Reconciliation% = (Used + Destroyed_coded + Destroyed_damaged + Returned_uncoded) / Issued × 100 ; Discrepancy = Issued − (Used + Destroyed + Returned). Also compare Used with units labeled.
calculations.notes: Limits: narrow preset limits based on historical data [21 CFR 211.125(c)]; EU Ch.4 4.21.

calculations.name: F0 (moist heat lethality)
calculations.formula: L(t) = 10^((T(t) − T_ref)/z) ; F0 = Σ L(t_i) × Δt (trapezoid integration), with z = 10 °C and T_ref = 121.1 °C (PDA TR1) or 121 °C (Ph. Eur. 5.1.1 / USP <1229.2>)
calculations.notes: Integration commonly starts and ends at a defined minimum temperature (e.g. 100 °C) [PDA TR1 Revised 2007 3.1.3]. 1 °C below reference gives L ≈ 0.79. 25.9 min at 116 °C ≈ F0 8 min [PDA TR1]. Ph. Eur. 5.1.1 requires minimum F0 ≥8 min at the slowest-to-heat position and minimum process temperature 110 °C. Make T_ref configurable per market/SOP and record it with the result.

calculations.name: Biological lethality and PNSU
calculations.formula: F_bio = D_121 × (log10 N0 − log10 N) [Ph. Eur. 5.1.1] ; log10 N_final = log10 N0 − F / D [USP <1229.2>] ; requirement: PNSU ≤ 10^-6
calculations.notes: N0 = bioburden per container (or BI population); D = D-value at reference temperature. Overkill = ≥12 log10 reduction of organisms with D ≥1 min [Annex 1 glossary].

calculations.name: Dry-heat depyrogenation equivalence (FD/FH)
calculations.notes: Annex 1 8.68: validation must show a suitable FH value and a minimum 3 log10 endotoxin reduction. USP <1228.1> (2024): confirmation samples NMT 0.1 EU per sample. Record the calculated FD for the coldest monitored position.

calculations.name: Bubble point (capillary) relation
calculations.formula: P_BP = 4 × k × γ × cosθ / d
calculations.notes: k = pore shape factor, γ = wetting-liquid surface tension, θ = contact angle, d = largest pore diameter. Explains why wetting fluid and temperature change BP, and hence why product-wet specs must be derived [PDA TR26 Revised 2025 Appendix I].

calculations.name: Product-wet integrity test specifications
calculations.formula: PBP_min = WBP_min × (PBP_avg / WBP_avg) ; TP_pw = MTP_ww × (PBP_avg / WBP_avg) ; DFL_pw = DFL_ww × (DF_pw / DF_ww)
calculations.notes: Pass criteria: measured BP ≥ PBP_min (or WBP_min if water-wet); diffusive flow at test pressure ≤ DFL. Diffusive-flow test pressure is typically ≤80% of BP. Specs must correlate to bacterial retention (B. diminuta ≥10^7 CFU/cm²) [PDA TR26 Revised 2025 7.4; Annex 1 8.87; FDA 2004 IX.B].

calculations.name: Diffusive flow vs pressure decay
calculations.formula: Fick: N = D × H × ΔP × φ / L ; approximate conversion: Q_diff (mL/min at ambient) ≈ (ΔP_decay / P_atm) × V_upstream / t
calculations.notes: V_upstream = upstream test volume (mL); t = test time (min); ΔP and P_atm in the same units. Example: 0.02 bar drop in 10 min, V = 500 mL → ≈0.99 mL/min. Exact exponential form in PDA TR26 Appendix II Eq. 14.

calculations.name: Lyophilizer leak rate
calculations.formula: Leak rate (mbar·L/s) = ΔP (mbar) × V_chamber+condenser (L) / Δt (s), measured with the chamber isolated at test vacuum
calculations.notes: Maximum permitted leakage specified and checked at the start of every cycle [Annex 1 8.124]; equipment-specific limit.

calculations.name: Endotoxin limit and maximum valid dilution
calculations.formula: EL = K / M ; MVD = (EL × C) / λ
calculations.notes: K = 5 EU/kg (non-intrathecal), 0.2 EU/kg (intrathecal); radiopharmaceuticals 175/V (intrathecal 14/V); per-m² products K = 100 EU/m². M = maximum bolus dose per kg (or maximum dose in one hour for infusions). C = sample concentration; λ = lysate sensitivity [USP <85>]. Body weight convention (70 kg per FDA Q&A 2012) not verified here.

calculations.name: Sterility test number of units (USP <71> Table 3, parenterals)
calculations.formula: n_per_medium = N ≤ 100: max(ceil(0.10 × N), 4) ; 100 < N ≤ 500: 10 ; N > 500: min(ceil(0.02 × N), 20) ; LVP: min(ceil(0.02 × N), 10) ; double n if one container cannot supply both media
calculations.notes: Quantity per medium per Table 2. Example: N = 12,000 vials of 5 mL → 20 per medium (2.5 mL each if split; otherwise 40 containers).

calculations.name: Visual inspection qualification metrics
calculations.formula: %PoD = (times rejected / times inspected) × 100 ; RZE = mean of %PoD over units with %PoD > 70% ; false reject rate target < 5%
calculations.notes: Reject zone ≥70% PoD, accept zone <30% PoD, gray zone 30-70% [USP <1790> 7.4-7.8].

calculations.name: AQL sampling lookup
calculations.formula: Sample size code letter = f(lot size, General Inspection Level II) from ANSI/ASQ Z1.4 (ISO 2859-1) Table I ; (n, Ac, Re) = f(code letter, AQL) from Table II-A (single, normal). Use n for the most critical category and the accept numbers for other categories at that n.
calculations.notes: Visible particulates AQL 0.65% [USP <790>]. Critical 0.010-0.10%, major 0.10-0.65%, minor 1.0-4.0% [USP <1790> Table 1]. Implement as a validated lookup table, not a formula.

calculations.name: Contamination recovery rate (EM trending)
calculations.formula: CRR% = (number of samples with any growth / total samples of that type and area in period) × 100
calculations.notes: USP <1116> suggested initial CRR: isolator/closed RABS <0.1%; ISO 5 <1%; ISO 6 <3%; ISO 7 <5%; ISO 8 <10% (per sample type).

calculations.name: Elapsed time vs time limits
calculations.formula: Elapsed = t_event_end − t_clock_start ; Remaining = Limit − Elapsed ; pre-alarm at Remaining ≤ X% of Limit
calculations.notes: Clocks per Annex 1 8.18(i)-(vii), 8.5, 8.36, 8.46; 21 CFR 211.111. Use a synchronized, trusted time source.

calculations.name: Cumulative time out of refrigeration (TOR)
calculations.formula: TOR_total = Σ (t_return_i − t_removal_i) for all excursions of a unit/tray/lot
calculations.notes: Limit from product stability data (product-specific; not a pharmacopoeial value).

edition_specific_features.feature: Sterility-assurance pre-start gate engine
edition_specific_features.why: Blocks batch start when APS coverage (line/process/shift/container bracket/speed/duration/personnel), cleanroom requalification, calibration, utilities release or EM readiness is missing. Removes the most common 'started anyway' loophole.

edition_specific_features.feature: Gowning qualification, APS participation and training check at room entry (badge/interlock integration), with maximum occupancy, supervised-entry workflow for unqualified persons, and automatic disqualification (adverse personnel-monitoring trend, failed APS)
edition_specific_features.why: Unsupervised Grade A/B access must be limited to qualified operators. Disqualification must be enforced, not just recorded.

edition_specific_features.feature: Intervention logging from an approved intervention catalogue: inherent/corrective, critical flag, maximum duration, units to remove, line clearance extent, required glove print/glove change. One-tap start/stop timestamps, operator attribution, box/tray number. Non-qualified interventions require prior QA e-authorization and auto-create a deviation
edition_specific_features.why: Interventions and stoppages must be in the batch record with time, duration and operators. Non-qualified ones need QU authorization and are considered at disposition. Same data feeds APS design (frequency and risk).
edition_specific_features.regulatory_basis: Annex 1 8.16-8.17, 9.25, 9.34, 9.47; FDA 2004 XII; PDA TR22 (Revised 2025) 4.1.3; FDA CP 7356.002A. https://www.fda.gov/media/71026/download

edition_specific_features.feature: EM integration and batch linkage: continuous Grade A/B particle stream with alert/action alarms; viable sample registration (location, time, method, media lot, operator) auto-linked to batch, room, zone and interventions; LIMS result import with species ID enforcement for A/B. Excursions automatically linked to every batch whose exposure window overlaps, including batches between monitoring and reporting
edition_specific_features.why: EM data must be reviewed for release, and excursions must be assessed for all impacted batches. Manual cross-referencing is error-prone at multi-site scale.
edition_specific_features.regulatory_basis: Annex 1 9.3, 9.13, 9.16-9.17, 9.24, 9.31, 10.10; FDA 2004 X.A, XII; PDA TR13 (Revised 2022). https://health.ec.europa.eu/system/files/2022-08/20220825_gmp-an1_en_0.pdf

edition_specific_features.feature: Multi-clock time-limit engine: T0 compounding → filtration → end of fill; sterile holds per item; decontaminated barrier hold; open-container exposure; filling time; lyo loading; time to terminal sterilization; settle-plate exposure ≤4 h; gown wear time; TOR. Pre-alarms, hard stops and automatic deviation on breach
edition_specific_features.why: Annex 1 requires defined and validated maxima for each aspect. 21 CFR 211.111 requires justified, documented deviations from time limits.
edition_specific_features.regulatory_basis: Annex 1 8.5, 8.18(i)-(vii), 8.36, 8.46, Table 6 note a; 21 CFR 211.111; FDA 2004 VIII. https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-211

edition_specific_features.feature: Item-level sterile status and hold-time tracking (electronic labels/RFID/barcodes) for sterilized parts, components, garments, SUS and trays, with states clean/sterile/expired/used and blocking of expired items at scan
edition_specific_features.why: Clear differentiation of sterilized from non-sterilized items and enforcement of maximum hold times. Electronic tracking is explicitly allowed.

edition_specific_features.feature: Sterilization/depyrogenation/decontamination/SIP cycle-record capture via equipment interfaces (OPC UA/SCADA). Unique cycle ID, recipe, setpoints vs actuals, independent monitor-probe data, automatic F0/FD computation, load-pattern verification against validated patterns, BI/CI results, chart/report attachment with checksum, review-by-exception, QA approval
edition_specific_features.why: Each cycle needs a unique identifier, and its conformity must be reviewed at certification. Batch records must document adherence to validated load patterns and any manual valve manipulations.

edition_specific_features.feature: Filter management: catalogue of validated filter trains, filter serial scanning, integrity-tester file import, PUPSIT/pre-use and post-use results, validated failure-analysis decision tree with maximum retest count, redundant/serial-train logic, vent/gas/lyophilizer filter tests, single-use/working-day limit, release gate
edition_specific_features.why: Filter integrity is a batch-release item. Retest loops are a classic data-integrity loophole unless they are proceduralized and counted.
edition_specific_features.regulatory_basis: Annex 1 6.19, 8.82(vi), 8.86-8.95, 8.124; FDA 2004 IX.B; PDA TR26 (Revised 2025) 7.5-7.6; Ph. Eur. 5.1.1. https://health.ec.europa.eu/system/files/2022-08/20220825_gmp-an1_en_0.pdf

edition_specific_features.feature: Fill weight/volume IPC module: balance/checkweigher integration, density-based volume conversion, per-needle sampling scheduler with overdue alarms, SPC charts, automatic 'units since last good check' segregation logic
edition_specific_features.why: Dose accuracy is a critical IPC and manual transcription is error-prone. Automated in-line weight checks also reduce Grade A interventions.
edition_specific_features.regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.110(a); FDA 2004 IV.E (on-line weight check reduces interventions); USP <697>, <1151>. https://www.fda.gov/media/71026/download

edition_specific_features.feature: Lyophilization data capture: recipe version, pre-cycle leak test, loading map (shelf/tray/probe), trends of shelf/product temperature and CM/Pirani pressure, alarms with acknowledgement, end-point determination, backfill/stoppering data, vent filter integrity; comparison to validated design space
edition_specific_features.why: The lyophilizer is an extension of aseptic processing. Leak rate and filter integrity are release items.

edition_specific_features.feature: Visual inspection module: inspector qualification/eye-test validity check, lux verification, pacing/rate capture, defect-library codes (critical/major/minor), AVI challenge scheduling, per-category alert/action limits, AQL plan calculator (Z1.4 GIL II), reinspection workflow with QA approval and tightened sampling, cross-batch defect trending
edition_specific_features.why: 100% inspection, defect trending and qualified inspectors are explicit requirements. Reinspection must be limited and controlled.

edition_specific_features.feature: CCI module: 100% results for fusion-sealed containers, sampling plans for others, method controls, vacuum-maintenance tests for vacuum-sealed containers, link to capping and crimp data
edition_specific_features.why: Fusion-sealed small containers need 100% integrity testing, and visual inspection is not an integrity test.

edition_specific_features.feature: Terminal sterilization load builder: single product lot and container size per load, validated pattern/min-max, sub-batch IDs, per-load sterility/bioburden samples at worst-case positions. Optional parametric-release configuration (load monitor and critical parameters as release criteria)
edition_specific_features.why: Loads define sub-batches for sterility testing. Parametric release replaces the sterility test with parameter compliance and needs rigorous data capture.
edition_specific_features.regulatory_basis: Annex 1 8.38, 8.54, 10.4, 10.6(ii); USP <1229.2> (2022), <1222>; FDA Parametric Release guidance (Feb 2010); EU Annex 17 (not verified here).

edition_specific_features.feature: Event-driven sampling planner: sterility samples at beginning/end and after critical interventions or excursions, per lyo load and per sub-batch, with USP <71> quantity calculator. Bioburden before final filter; reserve samples
edition_specific_features.why: Samples must represent the worst-case parts of the batch. Missing event-driven samples must block completion.

edition_specific_features.feature: Unit accountability engine across fill → lyo → capping → sterilization → inspection → packaging → serialization, with configurable limits and automatic deviation
edition_specific_features.why: Unexplained discrepancies (yield or counts) must be investigated before release. Units removed at interventions must match SOP counts.

edition_specific_features.feature: APS (media fill) record type. Reuses commercial building blocks plus APS-specific fields (worst-case design, intervention plan, media, incubation 7/14-day reads, reconciliation). Results update line/shift/operator qualifications. A failed APS triggers quarantine and impact review
edition_specific_features.why: PDA TR22 2025 expects the APS batch record to be electronic when commercial records are. Annex 1 9.46 prescribes actions on failure.

edition_specific_features.feature: Barrier-system records: isolator VHP cycles and decontamination hold, glove-port integrity at start/end of batch or campaign, isolator leak tests, RABS glove sterilization and open-door intervention log with post-exposure disinfection
edition_specific_features.why: Glove breaches and door openings are major contamination routes and must be traceable to batches.

edition_specific_features.feature: Alarm, event and utilities integration into the batch record: ΔP, HVAC, door interlocks, power disruptions, WFI TOC/conductivity, clean steam and gas monitoring. Critical alarms need immediate review and cannot be silently overridden
edition_specific_features.why: Support-system data and alarm reports are essential release elements, and any power disruption affecting quality must be in the batch record.

edition_specific_features.feature: Contamination-event impact analysis (genealogy/impact graph): from any event (EM action excursion, failed APS, failed sterilizer/SIP/tunnel cycle, failed filter integrity test, WFI excursion, HEPA failure, glove breach, operator disqualification) traverse to all potentially impacted batches, products and sites, then auto-quarantine unreleased stock and support recall decisions
edition_specific_features.why: Investigations must extend to other batches and products. For APS failures the scope may cross lines (e.g. a shared lyophilizer) or go back to all batches within expiry for intermittent faults. These are multi-hop, many-to-many traversals.

edition_specific_features.feature: Release/QP sterility-assurance dashboard auto-populated from the record: EM/trends, interventions, APS coverage, sterilization records, filter tests, bioburden, utilities, alarms, time limits, yields, VI/CCI, QC results. Hard gates before QU release or QP certification
edition_specific_features.why: Release persons must have access to all sterility-relevant information, and a holistic review must be documented.

edition_specific_features.feature: Market/region rule packs with strictest-applicable merge (EU/PIC/S vs US FDA and optional WHO/India). Covers PUPSIT expectation, APS acceptance criteria, EM limit tables (Grades A-D vs ISO 5-8), depyrogenation validation criterion, F0 reference temperature, visual inspection AQL, serialization (FMD vs DSCSA), labeling barcodes, QP vs QU release
edition_specific_features.why: One product may be supplied to several markets, and requirements differ in specific, known places.

edition_specific_features.feature: Cleanroom-appropriate UX: disinfectable/sporicide-resistant tablets and terminals supplied only for cleanroom use, large glove-friendly targets, scan-first entry (barcode/RFID), voice or foot-pedal event marking for interventions, no paper in Grade A/B, offline-tolerant execution with controlled re-synchronization
edition_specific_features.why: Paper and uncleanable devices add particle and microbial risk. Electronic devices are acceptable only if suitably designed for cleaning and disinfection, and fast entry reduces exposure time.
edition_specific_features.regulatory_basis: Annex 1 4.7, 7.9, 8.8; Annex 11 (2011) / 21 CFR Part 11 for records.

edition_specific_features.feature: CCS traceability: each master-record control (limit, frequency, hold time, intervention) references its CCS element and validation report. Change control flags CCS impact before and after implementation
edition_specific_features.why: The CCS must define critical control points and be kept up to date, and changes must be assessed for CCS impact.

edition_specific_features.feature: Injectable labeling and serialization controls: unit-label linear NDC barcode (US), ferrule/cap cautionary-statement rules, EU unique identifier plus anti-tampering device, DSCSA product identifier, aggregation, repository upload before release, serial reconciliation
edition_specific_features.why: Injectables are typically hospital-used and serialized, and label mix-ups on small vials and syringes are high-risk.

edition_specific_features.feature: Cold-chain / time-out-of-refrigeration tracking per tray/lot through inspection and packaging, with cumulative limits and stability-linked deviations
edition_specific_features.why: Many injectables (biologics, some small molecules) have strict excursion budgets, and inspection and packaging are the longest ambient exposures.
edition_specific_features.regulatory_basis: Annex 1 3.1(vi) (storage per registered conditions); product-specific stability data (no pharmacopoeial TOR limit exists).

edition_specific_features.feature: Review-by-exception for validated, continuously monitored steps (cycle data, EM streams) with non-suppressible escalation of sterility-critical exceptions
edition_specific_features.why: Reduces reviewer load at multi-site scale without hiding critical events. EU Chapter 4 allows exception-based automatic batch reports for validated, continuously monitored processes.
edition_specific_features.regulatory_basis: EU GMP Ch.4 note to 4.20 (per sibling research, not independently verified); Annex 1 5.2 (critical alarms reviewed immediately).

open_questions: DATA-MODEL NOTE for the user's question 'is a graph-based data structure or database a good idea for it?'. The injectables edition is where graph-shaped relationships concentrate. Typical many-to-many chains: (a) EM sample → room/zone/time window → all batches exposed, including batches produced between monitoring and reporting [Annex 1 9.13]; (b) APS run → line + process + shift + container bracket + shared equipment → all batches since the last successful APS. PDA TR22 (2025) says a lyophilizer-related failure spans every line using that unit, and intermittent faults can mean all batches within expiry. (c) Sterilizer/SIP/tunnel cycle → items and component lots in the load → many batches; (d) filter lot/serial → batches; (e) operator → interventions → batches (disqualification or glove-print hits); (f) WFI/clean-steam excursion → batches using that water since the last good result [Annex 1 6.12]; (g) isolator glove port → interventions made through it → batch. These are variable-depth (typically 2-6 hop) impact traversals that 21 CFR 211.192 and Annex 1 3.2 require to be complete and justified.

Recommendation to test in synthesis: keep the GMP system of record in an ACID relational or event-sourced store with Part 11/Annex 11 audit trails and e-signatures. Add a derived, rebuildable graph projection (a property-graph database or an in-database graph extension / recursive SQL) for impact analysis, genealogy and investigation UIs. A separate graph database as system of record would add validation burden, dual-write consistency risk and audit-trail complexity. Whether a derived graph index is itself GxP-relevant (it drives quarantine decisions) must be settled: if it drives automated quarantine, it needs validation (GAMP 5 category) and reconciliation checks against the system of record.
